question: Will exploratory coalition talks involving the CDU have publicly begun in Saxony-Anhalt by 17 September 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo (no CDU-party meeting reported) one day into a ~12-day window; ~12.5% of the window elapsed as of 2026-09-07T09:49Z. The CDU is second with 15 of 83 seats after collapsing from 37.1% to ~17-18%, is not the convening/plurality party (AfD 39 seats), and has no majority path that does not require both Die Linke (excluded by CDU incompatibility policy, restated by federal GS Hoppermann on 7 Sept) and BSW (whose federal leadership rules out backing a CDU-led government). It is simultaneously in a leadership crisis: Junge Union and ex-minister Feussner demand Schulze's resignation and a re-election of the entire state board; Schulze says the result must first be evaluated internally. Parties in an unresolved leadership fight and with no viable arithmetic rarely convene formal Sondierungen inside 11 days: in the two closest precedents (Saxony and Thuringia 2024, both AfD-plurality deadlocks) formal CDU Sondierungen began at ~day 27 and ~day 47, with only informal Kennenlerngespraeche by day 8 in Saxony. The 2021 Saxony-Anhalt fast start (day ~9) was a winner-with-options case, not analogous. Upside risks: very high salience, SPD/Linke publicly inviting the CDU to talk, a third-ballot arithmetic (44 anti-AfD vs 39 AfD) that rewards early coordination, and a low formal bar (one reported bilateral meeting with any party, e.g. CDU-SPD, suffices). No prediction market prices this event.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off reporting (MDR Sachsen-Anhalt or other credible media) that an actual MEETING between the CDU of Saxony-Anhalt and at least one other party in the new Landtag took place for the purpose of forming the next state government (Sondierung or Koalitionsverhandlung). It does NOT resolve off invitations, one-sided statements, internal CDU deliberations, or contacts not described as a meeting.

EVENT WINDOW: 6 Sept 2026 (election day, which itself does not count) -> end of 17 Sept 2026 local Magdeburg time (= 2026-09-17T22:00Z) per the criteria; as of Now 2026-09-07T09:49Z, ~12.5% elapsed. NOT derived from any forecasting-close time.

STATUS QUO AS OF NOW: no meeting between the CDU and any other party for government-formation purposes has been reported.

EVIDENCE (source, date):
- Result, 6 Sept 2026 (de.wikipedia 'Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt 2026'; dpa ROUNDUP 7 Sept via finanzen.net/ariva): AfD 43.8% (39 seats), CDU 17.2-18.3% depending on source (15 seats), SPD 9.3% (8), Gruene 8.9% (8), Linke 8.6% (8), BSW 5.3% (5), FDP 2.6% out. 83 seats total; 42 needed for a majority. Turnout 77.8%.
- Arithmetic (derived from the above): AfD+BSW = 44. CDU+SPD+Gruene+Linke+BSW = 44. CDU+SPD+Gruene+Linke = 39, equal to AfD alone. CDU+SPD+Gruene = 31. No two-party or three-party combination excluding the AfD reaches 42.
- dpa, 7 Sept 2026: AfD federal co-chair Chrupalla: 'Wir werden allen Parteien Gespraechsangebote machen'; talks 'sollten noch in dieser Woche anlaufen'. Spitzenkandidat Siegmund: 'Ich sehe aktuell keine Partner fuer eine Koalition', but says he does not know what the coming days bring.
- dpa/Deutschlandfunk, 6-7 Sept 2026: BSW state figure indicated the BSW could abstain in a third ballot, which under Saxony-Anhalt rules (relative majority in the third ballot) bears on whether Siegmund could be elected minister-president.
- Euronews, 6 Sept 2026: CDU's Schulze said the party must first 'auswerten' and 'verdauen' the result in its party bodies before determining coalition options. Linke's Reichinnek: willing to talk with 'demokratischen Kraeften', the CDU must decide 'auf welcher Seite der Geschichte sie steht'. SPD GS Kluessendorf: formation will be 'sehr, sehr schwierig' and urged the CDU not to rule out Die Linke. CDU federal GS Hoppermann: no points of contact with the AfD, and cooperation with Die Linke difficult given what she called its antisemitism problem.
- dpa/Volksstimme, 7 Sept 2026: CDU state leadership crisis. Schulze called the result 'richtig niederschmetternd'; the geschaeftsfuehrender Landesvorstand met Monday morning, Schulze then went to the CDU Bundesvorstand in Berlin, with the full Landesvorstand meeting again Monday evening, where he said he would present a 'Verfahrensvorschlag' whose content (incl. personnel consequences) he left open. Ex-education minister Eva Feussner demands his withdrawal; the Junge Union Sachsen-Anhalt demands his resignation plus a re-election of the entire state board.
- dpa, 7 Sept 2026: CDU federal leader/Chancellor Merz planned to comment publicly together with Schulze.
- Deciding-body calendar: the new Landtag must hold its constituent session by the 30th day after the election (6 Oct 2026, per the Landtag calendar cited in the question background). No legal deadline exists for Sondierungen or for the election of a minister-president; the caretaker Schulze cabinet remains in office meanwhile. No published CDU Landesparteitag date found.

BASE RATES / PRECEDENT TIMINGS (class stated for each):
- Over all German state elections since ~2014 (unconditional, formation-leading party): exploratory talks with at least one other party typically reported within roughly 4-14 days; e.g. Saxony-Anhalt 2021 (election 6 June, CDU won 37.1%): CDU exploratory talks with SPD/FDP/Gruene in the second week, roughly days 9-14, formal three-way negotiations early July, Haseloff re-elected 16 Sept 2021.
- Over the subclass 'AfD-plurality or deadlocked arithmetic, CDU as second party leading the anti-AfD attempt' (de.wikipedia articles on the 2024 Saxony and Thuringia elections): Saxony 2024 (election 1 Sept): 'Kennenlerngespraeche' between CDU, BSW and SPD from 9 Sept (day 8); party bodies only cleared the way for formal Sondierungen on 17-18 Oct (day ~47); BSW ended them 6 Nov. Thuringia 2024 (election 1 Sept): SPD state board accepted the invitation to Sondierungen on 23 Sept (day 22); joint CDU/BSW/SPD Sondierungen began 'Ende September' (day ~27+); Voigt elected minister-president 12 Dec 2024.
- Over the subclass 'plurality winner with one plausible partner in an AfD-strong east German state': Brandenburg 2024 (election 22 Sept): SPD-BSW exploratory talks began in the first days of October, roughly days 10-14.

EVIDENCE BOTH DIRECTIONS: toward talks happening soon — the anti-AfD parties together hold 44 of 83 and therefore a live third-ballot option, SPD and Linke have publicly invited the CDU to talk, the situation has exceptional national salience, and the bar is a single bilateral meeting with any one party (e.g. CDU-SPD), not a full multi-party round. Toward talks not happening soon — the CDU is not the convening party, its stated first step is internal evaluation, its leadership and possibly its whole state board are in question, its federal party rejects Die Linke and the AfD, the BSW's federal leadership rejects an anti-AfD all-party coalition, and no procedural deadline bites before the 6 Oct constituent session.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: any report of a scheduled or completed CDU meeting with another party; the outcome of the Monday-evening CDU Landesvorstand; a set date for the constituent session beyond the 6 Oct statutory deadline; a CDU Landesparteitag date; any prediction market or bookmaker contract on coalition-talk timing in Saxony-Anhalt (Polymarket had only a pre-election AfD vote-share market; Manifold search by the harness returned nothing; no Kalshi or bookmaker line located).

calls.reasoning: Base rate from German state elections is that first leadership-level talks come 3-14 days after the vote, but the relevant conditional class - AfD strongest, no viable arithmetic - is much slower (Saxony 2024: Kennenlerngespraeche day 8, formal Sondierungen day 46; Thuringia 2024: first Sondierungsrunde day 29). Saxony-Anhalt 2026 is harder than both: CDU+SPD+Gruene+Linke = 39 of 83 seats (42 needed) and BSW (5) publicly refuses any anti-AfD coalition, so the CDU has no majority partner to explore with, while it also excludes AfD and Linke by resolution. The CDU is simultaneously in a leadership crisis (Junge Union and Feussner demanding Schulze's and the entire state board's resignation), which historically freezes negotiating capacity for weeks. No deadline pressure before the 6 Oct constituent session. Upside risk: German norms produce early bilateral 'Gespraeche' and MDR could report a CDU-SPD/Gruene leadership meeting within the window that a resolver counts; also the criterion accepts any counterpart party. Only ~12% of the criteria window has elapsed as of Now, but the CDU's first week is committed to internal personnel decisions. No prediction market prices this event.

EVIDENCE - CONSTRAINTS ON CDU TALKS:
- CDU has standing party resolutions ruling out coalitions with BOTH the AfD and Die Linke; Schulze reaffirmed opposition to any cooperation with the AfD on 2026-09-07 (ZDFheute, dpa roundup 2026-09-07).
- BSW top candidate Thomas Schulze: BSW will not join a 'Brandmauer-Koalition' and will abstain in a third ballot if Siegmund stands for Minister President (Tagesspiegel liveblog, 2026-09-06/07).
- dpa background piece (2026-09-07) describes a five-party anti-AfD coalition as 'aeusserst ungewoehnlich, sehr kompliziert und kaum vorstellbar' and states no formal coalition negotiations are scheduled.
- Saxony-Anhalt constitution: in a third ballot for Minister President a plurality suffices.

EVIDENCE - CDU INTERNAL SITUATION:
- Schulze announced on election night he would put a 'Verfahrensvorschlag' to the CDU Landesvorstand on Monday evening 7 September; he left open whether it includes personal consequences (dpa, 2026-09-06/07).
- Junge Union Sachsen-Anhalt demands Schulze's resignation and re-election of the entire CDU state board; ex-minister Eva Feussner also demands his withdrawal (Volksstimme, ad-hoc-news, 2026-09-07).
- Sequence on 7 September: CDU state praesidium in the morning, federal party board in Berlin (Merz meeting Schulze publicly), state board in Magdeburg in the evening. Other parties' state boards also met in Magdeburg that evening.

EVIDENCE - COUNTERPARTY INITIATIVE:
- AfD co-chair Chrupalla: 'Wir werden Gespraechsangebote an alle Parteien senden. Dann sehen wir, wer unsere Hand wegschlaegt', and 'Wir muessen ins Gespraech kommen', addressed at the CDU (Handelsblatt/dpa, 2026-09-06).
- Siegmund (AfD) on 2026-09-07 claims a 'ganz klarer Regierungsauftrag', rules out toleration or minority arrangements as 'nicht stabil', and raises new elections as a fallback; AfD rejected BSW's idea of a cross-party Minister President.

BASE RATES - DAYS FROM ELECTION TO FIRST REPORTED INTER-PARTY MEETING:
- Over the sub-class 'AfD strongest, formation structurally blocked' (n=2 recent): Saxony 2024 (election 1 Sep) - CDU 'Kennenlerngespraeche' with potential partners began 9 September, day 8; party bodies only cleared formal Sondierungen on 17-18 October, day 46-47 (de.wikipedia Landtagswahl in Sachsen 2024). Thuringia 2024 (election 1 Sep) - first Sondierungsrunde of CDU, BSW and SPD took place Monday 30 September, day 29, with a second round on 2 October (ZDFheute, 2024-10-01).
- Over the sub-class 'CDU won and had a straightforward majority option': Saxony-Anhalt 2021 (election 6 Jun) - CDU announced on 7 June, day 1, that it would hold Sondierungen with SPD, FDP and Greens; FDP declared openness on 9 June, day 3; coalition-agreement draft agreed 9 August (de.wikipedia Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt 2021). Question background dates the actual first talks to the second week, roughly day 10-14.
- Over the broader class 'German state elections 2021-2024, largest non-excluded party': first exploratory meetings commonly fall day 3-14 (e.g. Brandenburg 2024, election 22 Sep, SPD-BSW Sondierungen from early October, roughly day 8-12; formal coalition talks cleared 28 October).

COMPARISON POINT ON LABELLING: in both 2024 cases the earliest CDU meetings were reported as 'Kennenlerngespraeche' or 'Gespraeche' and were explicitly distinguished by the participants from 'Sondierungen', which came weeks later after party bodies formally authorised them. This distinction between the two labels is what any resolution will turn on.

calls.dossier:
SUBJECT: Whether the CDU of Saxony-Anhalt holds at least one meeting reported as Sondierungsgespraeche or Koalitionsverhandlungen with another Landtag party, aimed at forming the next state government, on or before 17 Sept 2026 (Magdeburg local time).

EVENT WINDOW: 6 Sept 2026 (election day, excluded as a qualifying event) -> end of 17 Sept 2026 local, per the resolution criteria = approx. 12.0 days. As of Now (2026-09-07T09:49Z) approx. 12% elapsed; approx. 10.5 days remain.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: Resolves off reporting by MDR Sachsen-Anhalt or other credible sources that a MEETING between the CDU and at least one other Landtag party took place for government-formation purposes. Does NOT resolve off: internal CDU deliberations (party board, Fraktion, Landesparteitag), one-sided public statements or offers, or informal contacts not described as an actual meeting. Either Sondierungen or full Koalitionsverhandlungen qualify; the counterpart may be any Landtag party including the AfD.

RESULT AND ARITHMETIC (Wikipedia de/en, dpa/finanzen.net ROUNDUP, 2026-09-07):
- Landtag has 83 seats; absolute majority = 42. AfD 39 (43.8%, up from 20.8%/2021), CDU 15 (17.2%, down from 37.1%), SPD 8, Greens 8, Linke 8, BSW 5 (5.3%). FDP out at 2.5%. Turnout 77.8%.
- Combinations: CDU+SPD+Greens = 31. Plus Linke = 39. Plus BSW = 44. CDU+SPD+Greens+BSW = 36. No majority excluding the AfD exists without BOTH Linke and BSW.
- Under the state constitution the Minister President is elected in up to three ballots; ballots 1-2 need 42 of 83, ballot 3 needs only a plurality of votes cast with abstentions not counted. If a first ballot is held, the second must follow within 7 days. No legal deadline exists for holding the MP election at all; the caretaker Schulze cabinet (CDU/SPD/FDP, now without a majority) continues until a successor is elected.
- Constituent session of the 9th Landtag must occur by 6 Oct 2026 (30-day constitutional limit); no earlier date has been publicly fixed as of Now.

PARTY POSITIONS ON RECORD (all 6-7 Sept 2026 unless noted):
- AfD: Chrupalla, 'Wir werden allen Parteien Gespraechsangebote machen.' Siegmund speaks of a 'historic task', says he will extend a hand to 'every actor in the parliament', open to working 'with individual factions' or 'individual members of parliament'; explicitly rejects a toleration/abstention model: 'Enthaltung ist fuer mich keine stabile Mehrheit.' Siegmund will stand for Minister President.
- CDU state level: Schulze (13 Aug 2026, ZDF) ruled out AfD or Linke ministers in a cabinet he leads. After the vote he announced he would attend the federal board in Berlin and then put a 'Verfahrensvorschlag' to the CDU Saxony-Anhalt state board on the evening of Mon 7 Sept; he left personnel consequences open. Junge Union Saxony-Anhalt demands his resignation and re-election of the entire state leadership; ex-education minister Eva Feussner demands he resign the party chairmanship. The Harz district association, the state's largest, is reported as categorically rejecting 'Sondierungs-, Koalitions- oder Duldungsmodelle'.
- CDU federal level: a standing party resolution excludes coalitions with both AfD and Linke. Merz has said a situation 'similar to the minority Voigt cabinet in Thuringia' with tacit Linke support 'may be possible'. Amthor and Warken defended the federal course; Soeder called the result an 'epochal break' and urged the CDU to acknowledge the AfD's mandate.
- BSW: state lead candidate Thomas Schulze says BSW 'will offer everyone talks', will not join 'Brandmauer politics', and has floated abstaining on a third ballot in a way that could let Siegmund be elected; BSW has also proposed nominating a NON-PARTISAN (ueberparteilich) candidate for Minister President. Wagenknecht renewed a cooperation offer, said 'Die Brandmauer-Politik ist gescheitert', and separately said BSW would not join a bland all-party coalition whose only common denominator is opposition to the AfD.
- SPD/Greens/Linke: no publicly reported invitation to, or scheduling of, talks with the CDU as of Now.
- No party has publicly announced a date for any Sondierung with any other party as of Now.

BASE RATES — days from a German state election to the FIRST publicly reported Sondierung/coalition-negotiation meeting involving the party in question (compiled from Wikipedia election articles and party/press releases):
- Over ALL such elections since 2016, for the party that is the formateur (largest party or clear government-forming lead) WITH a viable arithmetic path: Schleswig-Holstein 2022 ~day 3-4; Lower Saxony 2022 ~day 4; NRW 2022 ~day 5-8; Bavaria 2023 ~day 4-6; Berlin repeat 2023 ~day 8-9; Hessen 2023 ~day 8-10; Brandenburg 2024 ~day 9-10; Saxony-Anhalt 2021 ~day 10-14. Roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of this subgroup are inside 11 days.
- Over the CONDITIONAL subgroup 'AfD-first or arithmetically blocked East German parliaments': Thuringia 2024 (election 1 Sept) — SPD state board accepted the invitation to Sondierungen with CDU and BSW on 23 Sept = day 22; the three parties' joint Sondierungen ran into a position paper published later. Thuringia 2019 (27 Oct) — first talks ~day 20. Saxony 2024 (1 Sept) — party executives of CDU, BSW and SPD cleared the way for Sondierungen on 17-18 Oct = day 46-47; SPD paused them 25 Oct; BSW ended them 6 Nov. In both 2024 East German cases the CDU was the formateur and still did not hold a formal Sondierung inside 11 days; earlier contacts in those cases were reported as Kennenlern-/Vorgespraeche.
- No published base rate was found for 'party that lost half its vote and has no arithmetic path opens Sondierungen within 11 days'; I could not find a compiled dataset of Sondierung start dates and constructed the above from individual election records.

calls.reference_class: German state (Landtag) elections since 2016: days from election day to the first publicly reported Sondierungsgespraech/coalition-negotiation meeting involving a given party, split by whether that party is the formateur with a viable arithmetic path

calls.reasoning: Status quo one day into an 11-day window: no CDU meeting with any party reported or scheduled. All three runs agree on the arithmetic (83 seats, 42 for majority; AfD 39, CDU 15; every non-AfD majority needs BOTH Linke, excluded by CDU resolution, and BSW, which publicly refuses anti-AfD coalitions) — and a 39-39 third-ballot tie is not a plurality, so no minority construction bypasses BSW either. The CDU is not the formateur; in the two closest analogues (Saxony 2024, Thuringia 2024) the CDU WAS formateur with a live path and still reached formal Sondierungen only at day ~46 and ~29, with day-8 contacts labelled Kennenlerngespraeche, which this fine print ('publicly and formally', informal contacts excluded) likely does not credit. Simultaneously the CDU's first week is committed to an internal leadership fight (JU and Feussner demanding Schulze's and the whole state board's resignation) that the criterion explicitly excludes, and the only forcing date, the 6 Oct constituent session, falls three weeks after the window closes. Upside kept live: one bilateral CDU-SPD meeting suffices, the two are still caretaker partners, and salience is extreme.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes were mostly judgment, not fact. Factual items settled from the dossiers: seat arithmetic is unanimous (only CDU vote share 17.2 vs 18.3% differs, immaterial at 15 seats); the Thuringia 2024 day-22 vs day-29 split is an announcement-vs-meeting distinction and both exceed 11 days; the Saxony-Anhalt 2021 'day 1' figure in Run 2 is an announcement of intent, the actual meeting was day ~10-14, so even the fastest favourable precedent only barely clears this window. Two disputes could NOT be settled without web access and are carried as uncertainty: the outcome of the CDU Landesvorstand meeting on the evening of 7 Sept (unknown to all three runs), and whether a resolver would credit a Kennenlern-/Vorgespraech as a formal Sondierung - the criterion's words 'publicly and formally' and its exclusion of informal contacts argue against, and in both 2024 analogues the participants themselves drew that line, so I discount but do not zero that pathway. On the pure judgment split I side with Run 3's structural reading over Runs 1-2's appeal to German fortnight norms: those norms are measured on formateur parties with a viable path, a class the CDU does not belong to here. I land at 0.18, below all but one run and below the pool, because the reconciled evidence stacks three independent brakes (no arithmetic path, contested own leadership, no forcing deadline before 6 Oct) against one cheap YES route (a CDU-SPD caretaker-partner bilateral reported as Sondierung). No market prices this event: all three runs independently checked Polymarket, Manifold and Kalshi and found only seat-share and next-government-composition contracts, none matching the timing question - I retrieved nothing myself this run.
